newsitem.title: USA: Unlikely Clinton will act in UPS strike.
newsitem.headline: Unlikely Clinton will act in UPS strike.

text.p: The White House reiterated on Tuesday that it is unlikely President Bill Clinton will intervene in the nation-wide strike against United Parcel Service because it does not pose a threat to the nation's economic health.

White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said Clinton did not have the authority to act under terms of the Taft-Hartley Act, which allows a president to intervene in a strike if it imperils the nation's economic health.
"We do not find that that standard has been met in this case and it seems unlikely given the structure of the industry that it will be met," McCurry said.

His statement echoed comments on Monday from the president and administration officials that Clinton was unlikely to intervene. Chief UPS negotiator Dave Murray said late Monday, after meeting with administration and union officials, that he would continue to lobby for White House action on the strike.
